ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
To improve traffic efficiency, many highway entrances and exits are equipped with Electronic Toll Collection (ETC) systems. Cars A and B exit the highway through the ETC lane and the Manual Toll Collection (MTC) lane, respectively, as shown in the diagram. Assume the speed bump is located at a distance $x = 60\,\mathrm{m}$ from the toll island entrance, and the total length of the toll island is $d = 40\,\mathrm{m}$. Both cars pass the speed bump simultaneously at the same speed $v_{1} = 72\,\mathrm{km/h}$, then decelerate uniformly with the same acceleration. Car A slows down to $v_{2} = 18\,\mathrm{km/h}$ and continues at a constant speed to the centerline to complete the payment, after which the automatic barrier opens to let it through. Car B comes to a stop exactly at the toll island's centerline payment window, takes $t_{0} = 20\,\mathrm{s}$ to complete the payment, and the manual barrier opens to let it through. Subsequently, both cars accelerate uniformly back to speed $v_{1}$ and continue driving at a constant speed along a straight line. The magnitudes of acceleration and deceleration are assumed to be equal.

1. The time difference between the manual toll lane and the ETC lane opening the barrier for passage.
2. The maximum distance between the two cars after they leave the toll station.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the vehicles travel from left to right, and on the left side is the speed bump (speed-reducing bump). The distance from the speed bump to the entrance of the toll island is marked as x = 60 m; the total length of the toll island is marked as d = 40 m. There is a vertical dashed line in the middle of the toll island, labeled Toll island centerline, indicating the centerline of the toll island, located at half of the length of the toll island. Car A is in the ETC Lane, and car B is in the MTC Channel. Reasoning: Take the speed bump as position s = 0, and the rightward direction as the positive direction. The toll island entrance is at s = 60 m, and the centerline is at s = 60 + d/2 = 60 + 20 = 80 m. The initial speed v1 = 72 km/h = 20 m/s, and the ETC low speed of car A v2 = 18 km/h = 5 m/s. Car B stops exactly from the speed bump to the centerline, with displacement L = 80 m. From 0 = v1^2 - 2aL, obtain a = v1^2/(2L) = 20^2/(2×80) = 2.5 m/s^2. The deceleration time of car B is t_B deceleration = 20/2.5 = 8 s, and then it pays for t0 = 20 s, so the opening time of the MTC barrier is t_B opening = 8 + 20 = 28 s. Car A uses the same deceleration to reduce from 20 m/s to 5 m/s, with time t_A deceleration = (20 - 5)/2.5 = 6 s, and deceleration displacement s_A deceleration = (20^2 - 5^2)/(2×2.5) = 75 m. At this time, 80 - 75 = 5 m remains from the centerline, and car A travels uniformly at 5 m/s for 1 s to the centerline, so the opening time of the ETC barrier is t_A opening = 6 + 1 = 7 s. Therefore, the time difference between the openings of the two barriers is 28 - 7 = 21 s. Continue to look at the maximum distance. At t = 7 s, A is at s = 80 m, with speed 5 m/s, and then accelerates to 20 m/s, requiring time (20 - 5)/2.5 = 6 s, namely to t = 13 s, the displacement increases by (5 + 20)/2 × 6 = 75 m, and the position is s_A = 155 m; afterward it travels uniformly at 20 m/s. Before t = 28 s, B is stopped at s = 80 m. At t = 28 s, it starts accelerating from 0 to 20 m/s, requiring 8 s. By t = 36 s, the displacement increases by 0.5×2.5×8^2 = 80 m, and the position is s_B = 160 m. At this time, A has also traveled uniformly from t = 13 s to t = 36 s for 20×23 = 460 m, and the position is s_A = 155 + 460 = 615 m. At this time, both vehicles have reached a speed of 20 m/s, and afterward the distance remains unchanged, so the maximum distance is 615 - 160 = 455 m.

method.method_draft: Use an event-by-event kinematics timeline with absolute positions. First read the diagram: the cars travel rightward from the speed bump; the toll-island entrance is x = 60 m from the speed bump; the island length is d = 40 m; the payment centerline is halfway through the island, so the distance from speed bump to centerline is L = x + d/2 = 80 m; A is in the ETC lane and B is in the MTC lane. From the text, convert v1 = 72 km/h = 20 m/s and v2 = 18 km/h = 5 m/s, note that B stops exactly at the centerline, A reaches the centerline at v2 and pays immediately, B waits t0 = 20 s, and acceleration/deceleration magnitudes are equal. Determine the common acceleration magnitude from B's braking over 80 m: 0 = v1^2 - 2aL. Then compute B's braking time and manual barrier opening time. Compute A's braking time and braking distance from 20 m/s to 5 m/s using the same a, then add the remaining constant-speed time to the centerline to get the ETC barrier opening time. Their difference gives 21 s. For the maximum separation, continue the absolute-position timeline after A opens: A accelerates from 5 to 20 m/s, then cruises; B remains stopped until its manual barrier opens, then accelerates from 0 to 20 m/s. Since separation increases until B also reaches 20 m/s and then remains constant, evaluate both cars' positions at the instant B finishes accelerating back to v1; the separation is 455 m.

B 车从减速带到中心线正好停止，位移 L = 80 m，由 0 = v1^2 - 2aL 得 a = v1^2/(2L) = 20^2/(2×80) = 2.5 m/s^2。B 车减速时间为 t_B减 = 20/2.5 = 8 s，再支付 t0 = 20 s，所以 MTC 栏杆开启时刻为 t_B开 = 8 + 20 = 28 s。

raw_record.original_question:
To improve traffic efficiency, many highway entrances and exits are equipped with Electronic Toll Collection (ETC) systems. Cars A and B exit the highway through the ETC lane and the Manual Toll Collection (MTC) lane, respectively, as shown in the diagram. Assume the speed bump is located at a distance $x = 60\,\mathrm{m}$ from the toll island entrance, and the total length of the toll island is $d = 40\,\mathrm{m}$. Both cars pass the speed bump simultaneously at the same speed $v_{1} = 72\,\mathrm{km/h}$, then decelerate uniformly with the same acceleration. Car A slows down to $v_{2} = 18\,\mathrm{km/h}$ and continues at a constant speed to the centerline to complete the payment, after which the automatic barrier opens to let it through. Car B comes to a stop exactly at the toll island's centerline payment window, takes $t_{0} = 20\,\mathrm{s}$ to complete the payment, and the manual barrier opens to let it through. Subsequently, both cars accelerate uniformly back to speed $v_{1}$ and continue driving at a constant speed along a straight line. The magnitudes of acceleration and deceleration are assumed to be equal.

1. The time difference between the manual toll lane and the ETC lane opening the barrier for passage.
2. The maximum distance between the two cars after they leave the toll station.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, the vehicles travel from left to right, and on the left side is the speed bump (speed-reducing bump). The distance from the speed bump to the entrance of the toll island is marked as x = 60 m; the total length of the toll island is marked as d = 40 m. There is a vertical dashed line in the middle of the toll island, labeled Toll island centerline, indicating the centerline of the toll island, located at half of the length of the toll island. Car A is in the ETC Lane, and car B is in the MTC Channel.

Reasoning: Take the speed bump as position s = 0, and the rightward direction as the positive direction. The toll island entrance is at s = 60 m, and the centerline is at s = 60 + d/2 = 60 + 20 = 80 m. The initial speed v1 = 72 km/h = 20 m/s, and the ETC low speed of car A v2 = 18 km/h = 5 m/s.

Car B stops exactly from the speed bump to the centerline, with displacement L = 80 m. From 0 = v1^2 - 2aL, obtain a = v1^2/(2L) = 20^2/(2×80) = 2.5 m/s^2. The deceleration time of car B is t_B deceleration = 20/2.5 = 8 s, and then it pays for t0 = 20 s, so the opening time of the MTC barrier is t_B opening = 8 + 20 = 28 s.

Car A uses the same deceleration to reduce from 20 m/s to 5 m/s, with time t_A deceleration = (20 - 5)/2.5 = 6 s, and deceleration displacement s_A deceleration = (20^2 - 5^2)/(2×2.5) = 75 m. At this time, 80 - 75 = 5 m remains from the centerline, and car A travels uniformly at 5 m/s for 1 s to the centerline, so the opening time of the ETC barrier is t_A opening = 6 + 1 = 7 s. Therefore, the time difference between the openings of the two barriers is 28 - 7 = 21 s.

Continue to look at the maximum distance. At t = 7 s, A is at s = 80 m, with speed 5 m/s, and then accelerates to 20 m/s, requiring time (20 - 5)/2.5 = 6 s, namely to t = 13 s, the displacement increases by (5 + 20)/2 × 6 = 75 m, and the position is s_A = 155 m; afterward it travels uniformly at 20 m/s. Before t = 28 s, B is stopped at s = 80 m. At t = 28 s, it starts accelerating from 0 to 20 m/s, requiring 8 s. By t = 36 s, the displacement increases by 0.5×2.5×8^2 = 80 m, and the position is s_B = 160 m. At this time, A has also traveled uniformly from t = 13 s to t = 36 s for 20×23 = 460 m, and the position is s_A = 155 + 460 = 615 m. At this time, both vehicles have reached a speed of 20 m/s, and afterward the distance remains unchanged, so the maximum distance is 615 - 160 = 455 m.
